subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: What authorization, retention, and storage boundary should Slack self-activity recall use when a DM/main session asks about the agent's own outbound channel sends?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the implementation decides who may learn about Slack channel activity from a DM and where retained outbound activity lives.

options.title: Narrow self-activity ledger
options.body: Record only agent-authored outbound Slack deliveries in a canonical store and expose authorized summaries to DM/main sessions.

options.title: Shared session grouping
options.body: Treat this as part of broader configurable shared Slack/Discord channel sessions, accepting larger context, migration, and privacy design work.

options.title: Document isolation
options.body: Keep current session isolation and document that operators must opt into broader session visibility or explicit memory workflows.

recommendation.title: Narrow self-activity ledger
recommendation.body: Record only agent-authored outbound Slack deliveries in a canonical store and expose authorized summaries to DM/main sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible combination of prior issue-review context and recent Slack/session/outbound routing history for this boundary decision.
